The date-range fix alone contributed ZERO Recall@10 improvement on this benchmark - included specifically to prevent misattribution. Do not cite this fix as a recall improvement.

This improvement is entirely attributable to the query compiler, not the date-fix (see pubmed_recall_at_10_live_api_date_fix_isolated). Even after this improvement, the resulting architecture (0.136 Recall@10, 0.059 MRR) was NOT selected - RAG (0.773 Recall@10, 0.636 MRR, unchanged/pre-existing) remains the frozen PubMed architecture. Fusion was evaluated and rejected (zero unique recall contribution from the live path).

not_a_percentage_claims: ChEMBL fuzzy-match fix: 0 misleading matches across 4 fabricated names in a fresh 10-case held-out supplement (was 1 confirmed false positive pre-fix) - a safety/correctness fix, not a recall metric.
All 7 Phase-4 hard safety gates pass on held-out, verified empirically.
accepted_limitations_not_fixed: ChEMBL search_by_target first-hit heuristic on ambiguous target names (3/21 dev+validation cases) - real entity returned, not fabricated, but not always the intended one.
PubMed RAG has no relevance-floor/zero-result path - always returns k=10 regardless of true relevance; pre-existing production behavior, not introduced by Phase 4.
non_comparable_claims: Any claim that Phase 4 'replaced' or 'upgraded' PubMed retrieval - RAG was validated, not changed.
Any claim that the multi-source coverage figure (0.571) reflects the final, fully-re-scored architecture - 2 of 3 remaining misses used the non-selected PubMed live-API path.
